title: A Radiators for the Inventory
premise: Gideon Montrose, a piano tuner who reads a house's history in the ticking of its radiators, has spent decades keeping an inventory of everything unsaid—notes tucked into piano benches, silences mapped room by room. When Marta Ilves, the last fluent speaker of a dying Baltic language, hires her to tune the piano in a house scheduled for demolition-sale, Marta asks Gideon to become her final student before the closing date. Learning the language forces Gideon to confront the summer her brother drowned and the words she never translated for their Estonian grandmother, and to return to the lakeside house where it happened. In the end, Gideon speaks the language aloud at the house's last gathering, carrying both grief and grammar forward, and chooses to stay visible.
about_author: Ansel Galloway is the pen name of a former building superintendent who spent twenty years listening to the pipes of old houses and writing about the people inside them. Their work has appeared in small literary journals, and this is their second novel.

chapters.title: The Inventory of Small Silences
chapters.summary: Gideon, tuning a piano in a condemned brownstone, catalogs the house's sounds and its unsaid things in her worn ledger. A referral card arrives: one job, an old woman, a house already sold. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: the comfort of invisibility, faintly cracked by loneliness.

chapters.title: Marta Ilves, Last Speaker
chapters.summary: Gideon meets Marta in the drafty lakeside house, where the radiators clank in a rhythm Gideon can't place. Marta agrees to the tuning on one condition: lessons, twice weekly, until the sale closes in ten weeks. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: wary curiosity tipping toward obligation.

chapters.title: First Words
chapters.summary: The first lesson: greetings, seasons, the word for thaw. Gideon recognizes sounds from her childhood—her grandmother's kitchen—and flinches from them. The radiator's clank resolves into something like a name. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: memory surfacing like a body in water.

chapters.title: What the Radiators Remember
chapters.summary: Gideon maps the house's heating system and realizes the pipes were installed the same year her family left the lake. Marta deflects questions about why she chose Gideon specifically. POV: Gideon, with a brief letter from Marta. Emotional beat: suspicion braided with longing.

chapters.title: The Drowned Summer
chapters.summary: Flashback: seventeen-year-old Gideon, her brother Toomas, the lake, the argument in a language she pretended not to understand, and the silence after. Present-day Gideon stops attending lessons. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: guilt hardening into avoidance.

chapters.title: An Empty Bench
chapters.summary: Gideon tunes other pianos, but every instrument now sounds wrong. She finds Marta's ledger—a mirror of her own inventory—listing Gideon's absences. The buyer's agent pressures Marta to vacate early. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: shame meeting its reflection.

chapters.title: Grammar of Forgiveness
chapters.summary: Gideon returns; Marta teaches her the conditional tense—the grammar of what might have been. Marta reveals she knew Gideon's grandmother, that the house was once hers, and that the drowning was not Gideon's doing. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: the first loosening of a thirty-year knot.

chapters.title: Closing Date
chapters.summary: The sale accelerates; movers arrive. Marta's health falters mid-lesson, and Gideon realizes the student must become the keeper. She records Marta speaking the old stories into her phone, hands shaking. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: terror of inheritance.

chapters.title: The House Speaks
chapters.summary: On the final night, Marta asks Gideon to drain the radiators herself—one last act of tuning. As the pipes go quiet, Gideon finally says aloud, in the old language, what she never said to Toomas. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: climax—grief spoken, not stored.

chapters.title: A New Inventory
chapters.summary: Weeks later: Marta lives with Gideon now; the house is sold but the language persists in a small class of three students. Gideon begins a new ledger—not of unsaid things, but of said ones. POV: Gideon. Emotional beat: belonging chosen at last, memory carried forward.
